claim: A single ticket to the Towers of La Rochelle costs EUR 9.50 (covering the Chaine and Lanterne towers); a combined EUR 15 ticket adds entry to one museum (Natural History, Maritime, or New World).
quote: Individual admission: EUR 9.50 for access to the Chaine and Lanterne towers ... Combined ticket: EUR 15 covers the towers plus one of these museums.

claim: Tour Saint-Nicolas (the urban dungeon / French Tower of Pisa) is closed for maintenance, while Tour de la Chaine (the tower that lost its roof) and Tour de la Lanterne (former lighthouse, prison and now art space, famous for its prisoner graffiti) remain open; all are remnants of medieval maritime fortifications offering panoramas of city and ocean.
quote: Tour Saint-Nicolas: Currently closed for maintenance ... 'the urban dungeon or French Tower of Pisa' ... Tour de la Lanterne ... 'lighthouse, prison and art' ... graffiti as notable features

claim: The Grosse-Horloge is a medieval fortified gateway with a square base topped by a campanile and ship-shaped weathervane, housing the bell Suzanne (installed 1478, 1.54 m diameter, 2.2 tonnes, the largest in the department), and marks the passage between the Vieux-Port and the old town's pedestrian streets.
quote: the structure features 'a square base topped by a campanile,' housing the bell Suzanne since 1478. The bell impressively measures 1.54 meters in diameter and weighs 2.2 tons - the department's largest. A ship-shaped weathervane crowns the tower.

claim: La Rochelle's Hotel de Ville, claimed as the oldest town hall still in use in France, was gutted by a fire on 28 June 2013 and reopened in December 2019 after a three-year restoration led by historic-monuments chief architect Philippe Villeneuve, revealing its Renaissance facade and Gothic ramparts.
quote: the building that claims the title of 'oldest town hall in France' ... celebrated its rebirth in December 2019, after three years of work ... restoration was carried out by the chief architect of Historic Monuments, Philippe Villeneuve

claim: The Hotel de Ville interior is seen only on a 45-minute guided tour (adults EUR 7, ages 6-11 EUR 6, free with La Rochelle Ocean Pass) covering the Gothic perimeter wall and belfry, Salle des Echevins, Salle des Fetes and Cabinet Jean Guiton with its legendary marble table; tours run Wednesdays and Thursdays at 3pm and 4pm, booking required.
quote: Adults: EUR 7.00 ... Children (6-11 years): EUR 6.00 ... Duration: 45 minutes ... Salle des Echevins (Aldermen's Hall), Salle des Fetes ... Cabinet Jean Guiton featuring its 'legendary marble table.' ... Wednesdays and Thursdays at 3pm and 4pm

claim: Aquarium de La Rochelle adult admission is €18.50 (€16.50 reduced), teens 13-17 €14.50, children 3-12 €12.50, under 3 free, and time-stamped online tickets are strongly advised to guarantee entry.
quote: Only the purchase of time-stamped tickets on our website ensures access to the visit on the day and at the time chosen.

claim: The Aquarium's official estimated visit duration is about 1.5 hours and it opens daily, with high-season hours (April-July) of 9am to 8pm (last entry 6:30pm).
quote: From Thursday, April 2 to Sunday, July 5, 2026, the Aquarium is open from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. (last entry at 6:30 p.m.)

claim: Tripadvisor reviewers commonly report spending about 2 hours, and up to 2-3 hours, to see the Aquarium fully.
quote: Multiple Tripadvisor reviews mention 'about 2 hours of visit'; some report it should take 'two to three hours to see it all'.

claim: The Musée Maritime de La Rochelle, whose heritage fleet includes the France 1 weather frigate and the Angoumois trawler, sells a combined ticket with the Towers of La Rochelle for €15, with free admission under 18 and on the first Sunday of each month outside July-August.
quote: A combined ticket costs 15€ (one entry to the Maritime Museum + the Towers of La Rochelle), with free admission for visitors under 18 ... Free entry for all visitors on the 1st Sunday of each month, except July-August.

claim: Le Bunker de La Rochelle, a preserved WWII U-boat officers' command bunker built secretly in the town centre in 1941, charges €7 adult and €5.50 child and opens daily 10am-6pm from April 2026.
quote: Les tarifs sont : adulte 7 euros et enfant 5,5 euros. ... le musée est ouvert tous les jours de 10h à 18h (dernières admissions).

claim: The Musée du Nouveau Monde (10 rue Fleuriau) costs €8 full / €5 reduced, opens Tuesday-Sunday 10h-12h30 and 13h30-17h30, closed Mondays; a 3-museum combined ticket including the Maritime Museum is €18 and a 3-month municipal pass-musées is €12.
quote: Musée du Nouveau Monde ... Admission Fees: €8 (full price), €5 (reduced) ... combined ticket for 3 museums ... €18 ... pass-musées (€12 full price – €8 reduced).

claim: The Musée d'Orbigny-Bernon (2 rue Saint-Côme) is a municipal museum priced at €8 full / €5 reduced with Tuesday-Sunday 10h-12h30 / 13h30-17h30 hours.
quote: Musée d'Orbigny-Bernon ... Tuesday to Sunday: 10h-12h30 / 13h30-17h30; Closed Mondays and public holidays ... €8 (full price), €5 (reduced).

claim: The Musée des Beaux-Arts de La Rochelle is closed for renovation works as of 2026 with no published reopening date.
quote: Le musée est actuellement fermé pour travaux.

claim: The Musée des Automates and Musée des Modèles Réduits closed on 5 November 2023 for relocation and have not published a reopening date or current status.
quote: Les Musées des Automates et des Modèles Réduits de La Rochelle ferment leurs portes à partir du 05/11/2023 pour déménagement ... Informations complémentaires à venir prochainement.

claim: Ile de Re bridge car (Class 1) toll is EUR 16 high season (15 Jun-15 Sep), EUR 8 medium season (2 Mar-14 Jun and 16 Sep-14 Nov), EUR 4 low season (15 Nov-1 Mar); motorcycles over 50cc EUR 3, under 50cc free.
quote: High season: €16 / Medium season: €8 / Low season: €4 ... High: du 15 juin au 15 septembre ... Medium: du 02 mars au 14 juin ... du 16 septembre au 14 novembre ... Low: du 15 novembre au 01 mars

claim: The Ile de Re bridge is 2.9265 km long, up to 42 m above sea level, and the toll is charged one way only (crossing to the island); the return is free, and non-motorized vehicles (bikes) cross free.
quote: 2.9265 km long with a maximum height of 42 meters above sea level ... The toll is charged one way only – when crossing from La Rochelle to the island. Return trips are free.

claim: Compagnie Inter-iles full Ile d'Aix + Fort Boyard + La Rochelle cruise costs (one-way) EUR 39.50 adult, EUR 34 student, EUR 26.50 child 4-17, EUR 6 under-4 and pets.
quote: Adults: €39.50 / Students: €34.00 / Children (4-17 years): €26.50 / Under 4 years: €6.00 / Pets: €6.00

claim: The Inter-iles Fort Boyard sea promenade from La Rochelle (Vieux Port) lasts roughly 2h-2h15, passing the La Rochelle towers and Minimes port through the Pertuis d'Antioche before approaching the fort.
quote: The cruise lasts approximately 2 hours to 2 hours 15 minutes ... the captain navigates through Pertuis d'Antioche, offering a magnificent panorama of islands including Aix, Ré, and Oléron before approaching Fort Boyard.

claim: The commented Fort Boyard tour with Compagnie Inter-iles departs La Rochelle's Vieux Port, runs daily 7 Feb-30 Nov 2026, lasts about 2 hours and is priced around EUR 29; reservations by phone 05 46 50 55 54.
quote: The tour operates from February 7th to November 30th, 2026, every day ... The price is 29 euros ... Reservations must be made by telephone with the Compagnie Interîles at 05 46 50 55 54.

claim: Regional bus Line 3/3E links La Rochelle to Saint-Martin-de-Re in about one hour, with single tickets EUR 2.50 and return EUR 4.50.
quote: daily buses (Line 3/3E) connecting La Rochelle to Saint-Martin-de-Ré. Single tickets cost €2.50 and return tickets €4.50. In one hour you'll arrive at Saint-Martin-de-Ré

claim: Ile de Re has around 138 km of cycle paths and a dedicated double cycle lane on the bridge; Saint-Martin-de-Re is fortified with UNESCO-listed Vauban defences and the Phare des Baleines is one of France's tallest lighthouses.
quote: With 138 kms of cycle paths and shared paths, the island of Ré is the ideal destination for safe cycling ... The bridge has a double lane reserved for cyclists, and passage is free for non-motorized vehicles.

claim: A maritime shuttle (Croisieres Interiles) links Ile de Re and La Rochelle in about an hour, carrying up to 30 bikes (reservation required), with bike crossing for around EUR 1 in summer.
quote: a shuttle service between Île de Ré and La Rochelle offers a crossing lasting around an hour. Their ship can accommodate up to 30 bikes ... the shuttle ferry allows you to cross with your bike from La Rochelle for only €1 during the summer season.

claim: Ile d'Oleron is reached by a free 2,862 m viaduct (23 m high, ~3 min crossing) from Bourcefranc-le-Chapus, open 24/7 and accessible to cyclists and pedestrians; the bridge turns 60 in 2026.
quote: The road bridge of Oléron Island is free, unlike that of the island of Ré. The bridge stretches over a length of 2,862 meters, 23 meters above the sea, and the crossing time is approximately 3 minutes ... inaugurated on June 21, 1966.

claim: Ile d'Oleron is about an hour to 1.5 hours' drive from La Rochelle and at 35 km long by 12 km wide is easily explored in a day.
quote: just over an hour's drive from La Rochelle ... at just 35km long and 12km wide, it really isn't that large. Its location halfway between Royan and La Rochelle makes it ideal for day trips

claim: Plage de la Concurrence is the most central beach, closest to the old port, with about 150m of sand along a promenade reachable from Parc Charruyer, supervised in summer.
quote: Plage de la Concurrence is the most central beach and closest to the old port. It features 150 meters of sand along a beautiful promenade... This beach is supervised in summer.

claim: Plage des Minimes sits between the marina and the Minimes peninsula, partly bordered by pine forest, with 200m of fine sand, summer beach volleyball, and views of Fort Boyard.
quote: In summer, beach volleyball courts are set up on this 200-meter fine sand beach. There are beautiful views of Fort Boyard and neighboring islands.

claim: La Rochelle pioneered free public bikes in 1976 (the little yellow bikes), evolving into a 24/7 self-service network in 2005, well before Paris or Lyon.
quote: La Rochelle launched the "little yellow bikes" in 1976, made available to everyone free of charge. In 2005, the program evolved into a full-fledged self-service bike network, accessible around the clock, well before Paris, Lyon, or other major cities.

claim: The Yélo self-service bike network has 760 bikes across 117 stations, runs 24/7, and costs EUR 1 for the first 30 minutes then EUR 1.50 per additional 30 minutes for occasional rental.
quote: 760 bikes... 117 stations... Accessible 7j/7, 24h/24... Occasional rental: €1 for first 30 minutes, then €1.50 per additional 30-minute period

claim: Navipromer runs cruises from La Rochelle's Old Port including a commented approach to Fort Boyard and crossings to Île d'Aix, where no motor vehicles are allowed.
quote: Navipromer Cruises operates family cruises departing from the Old Port of La Rochelle with excursions around Fort Boyard and maritime connections to Île d'Aix... no motor vehicles are allowed on the island.

claim: Canoe, kayak and stand-up paddle gear can be rented April to September from a base near the Salines bridge for trips on the calm Rompsay Canal.
quote: Equipment rental for canoes, kayaks, and stand-up paddleboards is available from April to September at a canoe base in La Rochelle, just before the Salines bridge.

claim: Tripadvisor lists SUP/kayak operators in La Rochelle including Aventure Weekngo Mer, Kayakomat La Rochelle (L'Houmeau) and TEX' Canoe.
quote: Aventure Weekngo Mer... Stand Up Paddleboarding • Kayaking & Canoeing... Kayakomat La Rochelle - L'houmeau... Self-Guided Tours & Rentals • Stand Up Paddleboarding... TEX' Canoe La Rochelle

claim: La Rochelle is on La Vélodyssée Atlantic cycle route; the 50km La Rochelle to Rochefort stage (about 3h20) starts opposite the port towers and runs via Châtelaillon-Plage along coastal paths.
quote: This is Stage 22 of 38 on La Vélodyssée, the Atlantic Cycling Route. The journey spans 50 kilometers... Starting "opposite the famous towers defending the port of La Rochelle," cyclists follow coastal paths to Châtelaillon-Plage.

claim: Île de Ré is reachable from La Rochelle via a dedicated cycle lane on the 2,926m bridge (free for non-motorised traffic) and has over 110km of mostly car-separated cycle paths linking its 10 villages.
quote: the 10 villages on the island are linked by a track... The island has over 110 km of cycle paths, most of them separated from cars... a sweeping 2926.5-metre feat of engineering... The bridge has a double lane reserved for cyclists, and passage is free for non-motorized vehicles.

claim: La Rochelle's Marché Central covered market is open daily 8:00am-1:30pm with an outdoor street market on Wednesday and Saturday from 7:30am, selling fish, seafood, cheese, foie gras, and regional wines/spirits.
quote: The Central Market operates every day from 8:00 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. The street market around the covered market runs Wednesday and Saturday from 7:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m.

claim: Marennes-Oléron oysters, finished in salt-marsh claires that give them a green tint, are the area's signature shellfish, and Charente-Maritime is France's leading oyster-producing region.
quote: Marennes-Oléron oysters are the local specialty, finished in salt ponds that give them a distinctive green tint and complex flavor.

claim: Mouclade is the Charentais signature dish of bouchot mussels (from the bay of Aiguillon near La Rochelle) cooked in white wine then bound in a creamy sauce seasoned with curry, turmeric, saffron and Pineau des Charentes.
quote: fleshy bouchot mussels 'La Charron' coming directly from the bay of Aiguillon ... Key seasonings include curry, turmeric, and saffron. Pineau des Charentes and butter are added before serving

claim: Pineau des Charentes is a PDO (AOC since 1945) liqueur wine made by stopping grape-must fermentation with cognac, and is France's leading liqueur wine.
quote: Pineau des Charentes, PDO since 1945 ... it is a liqueur wine, obtained when the fermentation of the grapes is stopped by the addition of alcohol. For Pineau, we use cognac.

claim: Bar André, on the Vieux-Port at 5 Rue Saint-Jean du Pérot, is a seafood brasserie founded in 1947 and now run by MOF chef Johan Leclerre, serving oysters, mussels and fish daily 9am-11pm.
quote: operating as 'a favorite meeting place for seamen' since its establishment in 1947 ... 5 Rue Saint Jean du Perot ... MOF chef Johan Leclerre ... oysters, mussels, and fish dishes

claim: La Yole de Chris is a modern seafood spot near the Vieux-Port linked to chef Christopher Coutanceau, with a boat-shaped bar serving oysters, seafood platters and fish carpaccio.
quote: La Yole de Chris - A trendy and modern spot located near the main house of Christopher Coutanceau ... boat-shaped bar. The menu focuses on elevated seafood dishes, including oysters, seafood platters, fish carpaccio

claim: The galette charentaise is a dense buttery cake sometimes flavoured with angelica, and the tourteau fromagé is a fresh-cheese cake recognizable by its blackened domed crust.
quote: The galette charentaise is a butter cake with a dense and soft texture, sometimes flavored with angelica. The tourteau fromager is recognizable by its black crust and light center made with fresh cheese.

claim: La Rochelle has dedicated shops and cellars for tasting and buying Pineau des Charentes, Cognac and regional wines.
quote: Pineau, Cognac and Wines in La Rochelle

claim: Direct TGV/OUIGO trains run Paris to La Rochelle (399 km) ~17 times a day, fastest in about 2h41m with no changes.
quote: the fastest services... it can take as little as 2 hours 41 minutes... around 17 trains per day running on this route, which spans 399 km. There's no need for any changes along the way, as there are direct trains available to La Rochelle.

claim: La Rochelle in June averages highs of 20.7C and lows of 14.8C, with ~9.6 hours of sun, 12.9 rain days and the longest daylight of the year at ~15h42m.
quote: average high temperatures of 20.7°C (69.3°F)... mean low temperature is 14.8°C (58.6°F)... rain falls for 12.9 days... average sunshine in June... is 9.6 hours, and June has the longest days of the year, with an average of 15 hours and 42 minutes of daylight.

claim: Sea temperature in early June is around 16.7C, rising to 18.4C by month's end (June average 18.1C).
quote: water temperatures start at around 16.7°C (62.1°F) in the first third of the month, rise to 17.5°C (63.5°F) mid-month, and reach 18.4°C (65.1°F) toward the end.

claim: The Passeur is a 3-minute on-demand electro-solar ferry across the Vieux-Port (Tour de la Chaine to Mediatheque) at 1.50 EUR; the Bus de Mer links Vieux-Port to Port des Minimes in 20 minutes at 3 EUR, running every 60 min off-season and every 30 min in July-August.
quote: Passeur... Connects the Vieux-Port (Tour de la Chaîne) with the Médiathèque... '3 minutes'... Single ticket costs €1.50... Bus de Mer... Links the Vieux-Port to Port des Minimes... '20 minutes'... Single ticket is €3... every 60 minutes off-season, every 30 minutes in July-August.

claim: La Rochelle-Ile de Re airport (LRH) is 5 km north of the city, served by Ryanair and easyJet to ~12 destinations including London Stansted/Gatwick, Bristol, Manchester, Dublin, Lyon, Marseille, Porto, Geneva and Marrakech.
quote: situated 5km from La Rochelle... Ryanair and easyJet being the only airlines operating... Dublin, Marseille and London Stansted are the 3 most popular routes... Bristol and London Gatwick via easyJet... Manchester via easyJet... Lyon via easyJet... Porto in Portugal and Geneva in Switzerland... Marrakech in Morocco via Ryanair

claim: On-street parking is 4 EUR for 2 hours (green zone, the max duration) or 9.50 EUR for 7.5 hours (orange hyper-center zone); free Sundays and holidays, with a 1 EUR/night Fri-Sun rate at Verdun and Vieux-Port Sud.
quote: green zone... €4 for two hours (the maximum authorized parking duration)... orange zone (hyper-center)... €9.50 for seven and a half hours... special rate of €1 per night (between 7pm and 6am) on all Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays... metered zones become free on Sundays and public holidays.

claim: Main visitor car parks include Vieux-Port Ouest (Saint-Jean-d'Acre, closest to the towers), Encan (by the aquarium), Verdun (city centre) and Saint-Nicolas; enclosed/underground parks give the first hour free Oct 1-Jun 30.
quote: Parking Vieux Port Ouest... closest to the towers and old port... Parking Encan... opposite the La Rochelle Aquarium... Parking Verdun... largest car parks in the city center... From October 1st to June 30th, the first hour of parking is free in enclosed and underground car parks.

claim: Best stay areas are the Vieux-Port (historic heart, close to towers/aquarium but busy), the Gabut (colourful former fishermen's quarter, quieter), lively Saint-Nicolas near the station, and upscale seaside La Genette; the city is compact, ~10 min on foot from station to Vieux-Port.
quote: Vieux-Port... historic and touristic heart... ideal area to stay... a very busy area in high season... Gabut... brightly painted wooden houses... relative tranquility even during peak tourist season... Saint-Nicolas is the liveliest neighborhood... after sunset... La Genette is the most sought-after neighborhood... 10 minutes on foot from the train station area to the Vieux-Port.
